daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

The illegal wiretapping scandal involving former National Police Chief Listyo Sigit Prabowo continued to dominate political headlines. Irjen Ahrie Sonta pledged to be transparent after being named a suspect in the case, with questions emerging about whether Listyo Sigit's network would resist the investigation. Investment Minister Bahlil Lahadalia denied involvement in wiretapping President Prabowo, while invoking loyalty and courage when discussing the matter. Current National Police Chief Suyudi asserted the police force remains solid despite the scandal.

  • Internal Golkar party tensions resurfaced as calls for an extraordinary congress re-emerged, with Bahlil commenting on political betrayal.
  • PDI-P chairwoman Megawati urged her party to remain critical in overseeing national and state life, while Hasto led PDI-P officials on a pilgrimage to Sukarno's grave ahead of Heroes Day.
  • Civil society organization Elsam called for an audit of the LIMS system following the illegal police wiretapping case.
  • Cabinet Secretary Teddy announced 265 "people's schools" had been established in 131 regions by October 2026.
  • Former Brimob commanders met with Police Chief Suyudi to discuss major personnel transfers and the wiretapping case.
  • NasDem party chairman Surya Paloh praised the enthusiasm of thousands who participated in the NasDem Run for Change event in Karawang.
  • PB Alkhairaat, an Islamic organization, voiced support for the president's steps to achieve national stability.

Foreign Policy & Defence

The Indonesian Navy recovered the black box from the Mi-17V5 helicopter that crashed while fighting forest fires in Central Kalimantan, with the head of BNPB attending the military funeral of personnel who died in the firefighting operations. Australian water bombers began operations to combat the fires in Kalimantan, with the Air Force designating Dhomber Air Base as the operational hub for Australian aircraft.

  • Former Vice President Jusuf Kalla departed for Turkey to discuss the Middle East crisis.
  • Indonesia intensified its diplomatic campaign to secure a seat on the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) Council.
  • The Indonesian Embassy in Singapore stepped up protection efforts for Indonesian seafarers working in the city-state.
  • Indonesia backed Saudi Arabia's crackdown on illegal Hajj pilgrimage brokers, with the Minister of Religious Affairs urging umrah pilgrims to be courteous in the Holy Land.
  • Indonesia strengthened border security through enhanced use of the Interpol alert system, while the police and KPAI bolstered coordination to protect children from crime.

Other

The Anti-Corruption Commission (KPK) confirmed that seizure of Rp 2 billion from KAI's CEO had occurred in August 2025 in connection with an ongoing investigation. Indonesia reported 72,336 workers had been laid off, highlighting ongoing employment challenges. Investment Minister Bahlil announced that subsidized fuel prices would not increase despite world oil prices exceeding Rp 20,000 per liter.

  • State investment firm Danareksa secured Rp 2.5 trillion in commitments from British and Dutch investors, while Indonesia sought deeper industrial and technology ties with Russia's Tatarstan region.
  • Barito Renewables completed the retrofit of Star Energy's Darajat Unit 3 geothermal facility, while Indonesia accelerated feasibility studies for a nuclear power plant in East Kalimantan.
  • Indonesia exceeded ozone elimination targets at the 38th Meeting of Parties in Kigali, and pitched biodiversity funding and fiscal reforms at the 17th Conference of Parties to the Convention on Biological Diversity.
  • Wait times for cornea transplants at RSCM could exceed one year due to limited eye donations.
  • Kediri's Dhoho Airport was officially designated as a regular Hajj embarkation point for 2027, and state railway operator KAI tested the eighth Commuter Line trainset with improvements over previous versions.
